Leaves that are burned do not drop saplings. Unlike most other leaves, pale oak leaves are always colored gray regardless of the [[biome]] they are placed in. They also do not become white during [[snowfall]]. === Smelting ingredient === {{Smelting |showname=1 |Pale Oak Leaves |Leaf Litter |0.1}} === Redstone component === {{Exclusive|java|section=1}} The state of a leaves block—including a player-placed block—changes after 1 game tick (half a redstone tick) when the distance to the nearest [[log]] or [[wood]] block changes, up to 6 blocks of leaves away. [[Observer]]s facing away from the leaves detect this change and transmit a redstone signal in the same game tick, making leaves useful for redstone signal transmission. === Piston interactivity === Leaves are destroyed when pushed by [[piston]]s. They do not stick to [[sticky piston]]s, [[slime block]]s, or [[honey block]]s. === Composting === Pale oak leaves have a 30% chance of increasing the compost level in a [[composter]] by 1. A stack of leaves yields an average of 3.05 [[bone meal]]. === Particles === [[File:Pale Oak Leaves particle example.png|Particles falling from pale oak leaves|thumb]] Pale oak leaves produce falling leaves [[particles]] underneath the leaf block, where they slowly fall to the ground. {{Infobox block |group=Unoxidized |group2=Exposed |group3=Weathered |group4=Oxidized |1-1=Copper Chest.gif |1-2=Large Copper Chest.gif |2-1=Exposed Copper Chest.gif |2-2=Large Exposed Copper Chest.gif |3-1=Weathered Copper Chest.gif |3-2=Large Weathered Copper Chest.gif |4-1=Oxidized Copper Chest.gif |4-2=Large Oxidized Copper Chest.gif |*-1caption=Single |*-2caption=Large |invimage=Copper Chest |invimage2=Exposed Copper Chest |invimage3=Weathered Copper Chest |invimage4=Oxidized Copper Chest |invimage5=Waxed Copper Chest |invimage6=Waxed Exposed Copper Chest |invimage7=Waxed Weathered Copper Chest |invimage8=Waxed Oxidized Copper Chest |invimage9=---- |invimage10=Copper Chest BE |invimage11=Exposed Copper Chest BE |invimage12=Weathered Copper Chest BE |invimage13=Oxidized Copper Chest BE |invimage14=Waxed Copper Chest BE |invimage15=Waxed Exposed Copper Chest BE |invimage16=Waxed Weathered Copper Chest BE |invimage17=Waxed Oxidized Copper Chest BE |transparent=Yes |light=No |tool=stone pickaxe |renewable=Yes |stackable=Yes (64) |flammable=No |lavasusceptible=No |waterloggable=Yes |mapcolor = * {{TooltipSprite||Copper Chest}} {{Map color|Block of Copper}} * {{TooltipSprite||Exposed Copper Chest}} {{Map color|Exposed Copper}} * {{TooltipSprite||Weathered Copper Chest}} {{Map color|Weathered Copper}} * {{TooltipSprite||Oxidized Copper Chest}} {{Map color|Oxidized Copper}} }} A '''copper chest''' is a type of [[chest]] made of [[copper]]. It functions almost identically to a normal wooden chest, except that it [[oxidize]]s over time, and [[copper golem]]s remove items from it to store inside nearby wooden chests. Like normal chests, two copper chests can merge into a '''large copper chest''' if placed adjacent each other. == Obtaining == === Breaking === A copper chest drops itself only if mined with a [[stone pickaxe]] or better. Using any other item to mine a copper chest drops only its contents. {{breaking row|horizontal=1|Copper Chest|Pickaxe|Stone}} === Crafting === {{Crafting |head=1 |A1=Copper Ingot |A2=Copper Ingot |A3=Copper Ingot |B1=Copper Ingot |B2=Chest |B3=Copper Ingot |C1=Copper Ingot |C2=Copper Ingot |C3=Copper Ingot |Output=Copper Chest |type=Decoration block }} {{Crafting |Matching Unwaxed Copper Chest |Honeycomb |Output=Matching Waxed Copper Chest |type=Decoration block |foot=1 }} === Natural generation === Oxidized copper chests can generate as part of [[abandoned camp]]s. === Post-generation === {{main|Copper Golem#Spawning}} Upon creating a [[copper golem]] by placing a [[carved pumpkin]] or [[jack o'lantern]] next to a [[block of copper]], a copper chest is generated at the location of the copper block. Both the chest and the golem are spawned with their [[oxidation]] state matching that of the block of copper, but do not generate [[waxing|waxed]] even when a waxed block of copper is used. == Usage == [[File:Copper golem searches copper chest.png|thumb|A copper golem opens a copper chest to search for items to pick up.]] A copper chest placed adjacent to another copper chest joins to create a large copper chest. Two adjacent copper chests merge into a large copper chest even if the two chests have different oxidization levels or waxed states; in such cases, the resulting large chest takes the oxidization level of the least oxidized half, and is unwaxed if one of the two halves is unwaxed.{{bug|MC-300050||Placing different copper chests next to each other combines them into a large copper chest|WAI}} A player can prevent the formation of a large chest, and place two small copper chests side by side, by {{control|sneaking|sneak}} while placing the second chest {{in|java}}, pushing a copper chest into place with a [[piston]] {{in|bedrock}}, or placing the second chest facing a different direction from the first chest. {{IN|java}}, copper chests cannot be moved by [[piston]]s, and [[sticky pistons]]. === Copper golem === {{main|Copper Golem#Chest interactions and item transportation}} If a copper golem is not holding an item, it visits up to 10 copper chests (regardless of their oxidization or waxed status) in sequence to try to take out up to 16 of the first item contained within. The search area for copper chests from the copper golem's position is 32 blocks horizontally and 8 blocks vertically.{{Info needed|Is it taxicab or euclidian?}} === Container === A copper chest can be used as a container and has 27 slots of inventory space, and a large copper chest has twice that amount, at 54 slots. In the ''Java Edition'' interface, the top three rows for a large copper chest correspond to the left half of the copper chest when facing it, and the bottom three rows correspond to the right half. In ''Bedrock Edition'', the top three rows correspond to whichever half was placed first and the bottom three to the other half. Copper chests open when {{ctrl|used}}. To move items between the copper chest inventory and the player inventory or hotbar while the copper chest GUI is open, drag or shift-click the items. {{IN|java}}, holding {{key|Shift}} and double-clicking while holding an item moves all items of the type clicked on in or out of the copper chest, to the extent that space is available for them. To exit the copper chest GUI, use the {{key|Escape}} control. A copper chest cannot be opened if there is a [[conductive]] block above it ({{in|bedrock|lc=}}, bottom slabs prevent copper chests from being opened). Solid faces do not prevent copper chests from opening, so the lid of the copper chest can phase through blocks such as bottom-half [[slab]]s{{only|JE}}, [[stairs]], and [[non-conductive]] full cubes such as [[glass]] and [[ice]]. [[Cat]]s sitting on copper chests prevent them from opening. Because copper chests themselves are non-conductive, two copper chests can be stacked on top of one another while still allowing the lower copper chest to be opened. Players can open copper chests when they are being hurt ([[effect]] of Instant Damage, Poison, Wither, on fire, damaged by other [[player]]s or [[mob]]s, etc.). By default, the GUI of a copper chest is labeled "Copper Chest"{{only|be|short=1}}/"Chest"{{only|je|short=1}} and the GUI of a large copper chest is labeled "Large Copper Chest"{{only|be|short=1}}/"Large Chest".{{only|je|short=1}} A copper chest's GUI label can be changed by naming the chest in an [[anvil]] before placing it, or, {{in|java}}, by using the {{cmd|data}} command (for example, to label a chest at (0,64,0) as "Bonus Chest!", use {{cmd|data merge block 0 64 0 {CustomName:'"Bonus Chest!"'}}}). If half of a large copper chest is renamed, that name is used to label the GUI of the entire large copper chest, but if the named half is destroyed the other half reverts to the default label. If both halves of a large copper chest have different names, the GUI uses the name of the northernmost or westernmost half. {{IN|java}}, a copper chest can be "locked" by setting its {{nbt|compound|lock}} tag using the {{cmd|data}} command. If a chest's {{nbt|compound|lock}} tag is not blank, the copper chest cannot be opened unless the player is holding an item with the same name as the lock tag's text. For example, to lock a copper chest at (0,64,0) so that the copper chest cannot be opened unless the player is holding an item named "Copper Chest Key", use {{cmd|data merge block 0 64 0 {lock:{components:{"custom_name":"Copper Chest Key"}}}}}. === Oxidation === {{main|Oxidation}} Non-waxed copper chests have four stages of oxidation (including the initial normal state). [[Lightning bolt]]s, and using an [[axe]] while sneaking can remove the oxidation on copper chests. Using a [[honeycomb]] on a copper chest prevents it from oxidizing. As the block begins to oxidize (exposed), it gets discolored and green spots begin to appear. As the oxidation continues (weathered), the block is a green color with brown spots. In the last stage (oxidized), the block is teal with several green spots. === Piglins === [[Piglin]]s become hostile toward players who open or break a copper chest. == Sounds == === Generic === A copper golem statue retains its pose when broken. [[File:Copper golem statue poses inventory.png|thumb|200px|All the copper golem statue poses in the [[inventory]]]] {{breaking row |horizontal=1 |link=none |Copper Golem Statue |Pickaxe}} === Natural generation === An oxidized copper golem statue generates in [[abandoned camp]]s. === Post-generation === Once fully oxidized, a [[copper golem]] has a 0.58% chance per [[tick]] to become a copper golem statue and take a random pose, provided it is not [[waxed]] and is fully located in [[air]] (that is, a copper golem cannot turn into a statue while underwater or standing on a partial block such as a [[slab]], as part of its hitbox is not located within an air block). This process takes 8.62 seconds on average. During the transformation, any items held by the copper golem are [[drops|dropped]]. == Usage == === Posing === {{control|Interacting}} with a copper golem statue changes its pose, cycling through four poses: standing, sitting, running, and star. {{IN|bedrock}}, the player's hand must be empty in order to cycle through poses. As the block begins to oxidize (exposed), it gets discolored and green spots begin to appear. As the oxidation continues (weathered), the block is a green color with brown spots. In the last stage (oxidized), the block is teal with several green spots. === Reanimation === Using an axe on an unoxidized unwaxed copper golem statue reanimates it into an unoxidized unwaxed [[copper golem]]. === Piston interactivity === Copper golem statues break when pushed by [[piston]]s, cannot be pulled by them and they don't stick to [[slime block]]s or [[honey block]]s. === Redstone component === A [[redstone comparator]] can read the state of a copper golem statue and emit a signal strength based on its pose. {| class="wikitable" ! A '''copper chain''' is an oxidizing directional [[block]] and the [[copper]] variant of [[chain]]s.

== Obtaining ==
=== Breaking ===
Copper chains can be mined using any [[pickaxe]]. If mined without a pickaxe, they drop nothing.

== Usage ==
{{for|information about the placement mechanics of all chains|Chain#Usage}}
Copper chains share much of their functionality with their iron counterparts.

=== Oxidation ===
{{main|Oxidation}}
Non-waxed copper chains have four stages of oxidation (including the initial normal state). [[Lightning bolt]]s and [[axe]]s can remove the oxidation on copper chains. They can be waxed with [[honeycomb]] to prevent oxidation from progressing.

As the block begins to oxidize (exposed), it gets discolored and green spots begin to appear. As the oxidation continues (weathered), the block is a green color with brown spots. In the last stage (oxidized), the block is teal with several green spots.

'''Copper bars''' are [[copper]] variants of [[bars]]. Unlike [[iron bars]], they are colored copper orange and can [[oxidize]] over time, similar to other copper blocks.

== Obtaining ==

Copper bars can be mined using any [[pickaxe]]. If mined without a pickaxe, nothing is dropped.

=== Waxing ===
Like other copper blocks, the waxed variant can be obtained by {{Control|using}} a [[honeycomb]] item on the block.

== Usage ==
{{for|information about the placement mechanics of all bars|Bars#Usage}}

=== Oxidation ===
{{main|Oxidation}}
Non-waxed copper bars have four stages of oxidation (including the initial normal state). [[Lightning bolt]]s and [[axe]]s can remove the oxidation on copper bars. They can be waxed with [[honeycomb]] to prevent oxidation from progressing.

As the block begins to oxidize (exposed), it gets discolored and green spots begin to appear. As the oxidation continues (weathered), the block is a green color with brown spots. In the last stage (oxidized), the block is teal with several green spots.

A '''copper lantern''' is a [[copper]] variant of a [[lantern]] that displays a green flame and oxidizes over time.

== Obtaining ==
=== Breaking ===
A copper lantern can be mined with anything, but [[pickaxe]]s are the fastest. A copper lantern also breaks and drops itself if a [[piston]] extends or pushes a block into its location, or if its supporting block is moved or destroyed.

=== Natural generation ===
An oxidized copper lantern is generated in [[abandoned camp]]s.

== Usage ==
{{Main|Opacity/Placement}}Similarly to other types of lanterns, copper lanterns can either be placed on top of, or hung from, the surfaces of most solid blocks (though some blocks will require sneaking).

To place a copper lantern on top of a block, aim at the block's top face, and press use. To hang a copper lantern from the bottom of a block, aim at the block's bottom face, and press use. Also similarly to other lanterns, if a copper lantern is hung from the bottom face of a chain, the lantern and the chain will connect seamlessly.

Soul lanterns can also be placed by pressing use on a block adjacent to an air block the copper lantern could occupy, much like other types of lantern. Pressing use on the top half of the adjacent block will hang the lantern from the bottom of an above block, and pressing use on the bottom half of the adjacent block will place the lantern down on the top face of a bottom block.

Like other types of lantern, if a copper lantern exists on an invalid surface (a surface where the copper lantern could not normally be placed on), the copper lantern will break and drop itself, upon the invalid surface receiving a block update.

=== Light ===
The copper lantern is among the [[Light#Light-emitting blocks|most luminous of light sources]], emitting a light level of 15. Copper lanterns also melt [[Snow layer|snow layers]] within 2 blocks and [[ice]] within 3 blocks ([[taxicab distance]]).

When the [[Render Dragon Features for Creators]] experiment is enabled in ''[[Minecraft Preview]]'', the inside of all copper lanterns emits colored [[Vibrant Visuals#Point lighting|point lighting]] with {{Color|#86ca59}} for the unaffected unwaxed variant, and {{Color|#e8c398}} for all other variants. The casing of the copper lantern blocks a part of the light and casts some shadows around the lantern.

=== Oxidation ===
{{main|Oxidation}}
Non-waxed copper lanterns have four stages of oxidation (including the initial normal state). [[Lightning bolt]]s and [[axe]]s can remove the oxidation on copper lanterns. Using a [[honeycomb]] on a copper lantern prevents it from oxidizing.

As the block begins to oxidize (exposed), it gets discolored and green spots begin to appear. As the oxidation continues (weathered), the block is a green color with brown spots. In the last stage (oxidized), the block is teal with several green spots.

Unlike [[copper bulb]]s, the light level of a copper lantern is unaffected by its oxidation stage; even an oxidized copper lantern will still emit a light level of 15.

'''{{BE|short=1}}''': Guitar {{upcoming|26.60}} }} '''Wool stairs''' are a craftable [[stair]] variant of [[wool]]. They can be [[dye]]d in all 16 colors. == Obtaining == === Breaking === Wool stairs can be broken using any [[tool]], but [[shears]] are the fastest. {{breaking row|horizontal=1|Wool Stairs|shears=1}} === Natural generation === White wool stairs generate naturally as part of structures within [[abandoned camp]]s. === Crafting === {{Crafting |head=1 |A1= Matching Wool |A2= Matching Wool |B2= Matching Wool |A3= Matching Wool |B3= Matching Wool |C3= Matching Wool |Output= Matching Wool Stairs,4 |type= Building block }} {{Crafting |Any Wool Stairs |Matching Dye |Output=Matching Wool Stairs |type=Building block |foot=1 }} == Usage == {{for|information about the placement mechanics of all stairs|Stairs#Usage}} Wool stairs come in sixteen colors, which are white, light gray, gray, black, brown, red, orange, yellow, lime, green, cyan, light blue, blue, purple, magenta, and pink. Just like the wool block, the white variant serves as the undyed block. Wool stairs of any color can be re-dyed into any other color. Wool stairs are easily mined, highly flammable, and offer little resistance against [[explosion]]s. === Vibration occlusion === Contrary to popular belief, wool stairs cannot be used to block [[vibration]]s from reaching nearby [[sculk sensor]]s. If wool stairs are placed between a sensor and a vibration source, the sensor is somehow still able to detect vibrations behind it. If wool stairs are placed between a sensor and a [[sculk shrieker]], the sensor is able to alert the shrieker. This also applies to [[Allay|allays]] hearing note blocks and [[Warden|wardens]] hearing sounds. Although they don't work for occluding, sculk sensors are not able to detect the placing and breaking of wool stairs, as well as entities [[walking]], [[sprinting]], or [[jumping]] on top of it. They are also unable to detect [[Item (entity)|items]] dropped on wool stairs, or wool stairs itself dropped in item form. === Fuel === {{IN|Java}}, wool stairs can be used as fuel in [[furnace]]s and [[Furnace (disambiguation)|their variants]], smelting 0.5 items per block of wool stairs. == Sounds == {{Sound table/Block/Wool}} == Data values == === ID === {{JE}}: {{ID table |edition=java '''{{BE|short=1}}''': Guitar {{upcoming|26.60}} }} A '''wool slab''' is a craftable [[slab]] variant of [[wool]]. It can be [[dye]]d in all 16 colors. == Obtaining == === Breaking === Wool slabs can be broken using any [[tool]], but [[shears]] are the fastest. {{breaking row|horizontal=1|Wool Slab|shears=1}} === Crafting === {{Crafting |head=1 |A3= Matching Wool |B3= Matching Wool |C3= Matching Wool |Output= Matching Wool Slab,6 |type= Building block }} {{Crafting |Any Wool Slab |Matching Dye |Output=Matching Wool Slab |type=Building block |foot=1 }} == Usage == {{for|information about the placement mechanics of all slabs|Slab#Usage}}Wool slabs come in sixteen colors, which are white, light gray, gray, black, brown, red, orange, yellow, lime, green, cyan, light blue, blue, purple, magenta, and pink. Just like the wool block, the white variant serves as the undyed block. Wool slabs of any color can be re-dyed into any other color, just like [[wool]] can be re-dyed. Wool slabs are easily mined, highly flammable, and offer little resistance against [[explosion]]s. === Crafting ingredient === {{crafting usage|Matching Wool Slab,Any Wool Slab}} === Vibration occlusion === Contrary to popular belief, wool slabs cannot be used to block [[Vibration|vibrations]] from reaching nearby [[Sculk sensor|sculk sensors]]. If wool slabs are placed between a sensor and a vibration source, the sensor is somehow still able to detect vibrations behind it. If wool slabs are placed between a sensor and a [[sculk shrieker]], the sensor is able to alert the shrieker. This also applies to [[Allay|allays]] hearing note blocks and [[Warden|wardens]] hearing sounds. If two wool slabs are stacked to make a [[Slab#Placement|block]], the vibrations can still pass through to the [[Sculk Sensor|sculk sensor]]. Although they don't work for occluding, sculk sensors are not able to detect the placing and breaking of wool slabs, as well as entities [[walking]], [[sprinting]], or [[jumping]] on top of it. They are also unable to detect [[Item (entity)|items]] dropped on wool slabs, or wool slabs itself dropped in item form. === Fuel === {{IN|Java}}, wool slabs can be used as fuel in furnaces and their variants, smelting 0.25 items per wool slab, which is 4 wool slabs per item. == Sounds == {{Sound table/Block/Wool}} == Data values == === ID === {{JE}}: {{ID table |edition=java |spritetype=block
